title: Carl DeMaio urges support for California Voter ID Initiative as deadline nears - San Diego City Wire
text:
Carl DeMaio, a political commentator and activist in California, posted several updates on his social media accounts regarding the ongoing campaign for the California Voter ID Initiative. In a post dated December 2, 2025, DeMaio announced a milestone in the signature collection process: “BREAKING: We just crossed 700,000 signatures for the CA Voter ID Initiative — but we still need 300,000 more by December 31! I’m calling on every Californian who cares about election integrity: we need your help NOW.”
Later that day, DeMaio provided further instructions to supporters on how to participate in the petition effort. On December 2, 2025, he posted: “Download, print, sign and mail back the petition at https://t.co/2M08edor5s”.
On December 3, 2025, DeMaio addressed media coverage of welfare fraud scandals involving state governors. He stated: “National news media is making a big deal over the welfare fraud scandal involving Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, but not the more significant welfare fraud happening here in CA under Gavin Newsom! Learn why — WATCH! https://t.co/2F1Qaf3x86”
DeMaio has been an advocate for voter identification requirements in California. The initiative referenced seeks to require voters to present identification at polling places or when voting by mail. Supporters argue this would enhance election security and public confidence in electoral outcomes. Opponents contend that such measures could restrict access for eligible voters without government-issued identification.
The campaign’s deadline for collecting signatures is December 31, as required by California’s ballot initiative process. If enough valid signatures are gathered and verified by state officials, the measure may appear on a future statewide ballot.
Welfare fraud has been a topic of debate both nationally and within California politics. High-profile cases have prompted scrutiny of oversight practices and administrative controls under current state leadership.
